variables.description: User-defined variables for use in jz/mu_r formulas. Values can be numbers or formulas (quotes optional). Variables can reference previously defined variables using $varname syntax. Reserved names: step, H, dx, dy, dr, dtheta, N, A, pi, e
variables.example:
variables:
  freq: 60
  omega: 2*pi*freq  # Can reference $freq
  rpm: freq/60      # Quotes optional for formulas

omp.description: OpenMP runtime configuration. threads <= 0 or omitted uses the runtime/system default.

threads.description: Maximum OpenMP thread count. 0 or omitted uses all threads selected by the OpenMP runtime.

polar_domain.example:
polar_domain:
  r_start: 0.222
  r_end: 0.278
  r_orientation: horizontal
  theta_range: 1.0471975512  # pi/3

r_start.description: Inner radius in METRES (physical, not pixels), 0 <= r_start < r_end. r_start: 0 means the domain includes the rotor axis (a full disc) and requires inner: dirichlet. The image's r-axis pixels map linearly onto [r_start, r_end].

r_end.description: Outer radius in METRES (physical, not pixels)

theta_range.description: Angular range [rad], typically π/n for n-pole sector models

polar_boundary_conditions.description: Boundary conditions for polar coordinates (radial: inner/outer, angular: theta_min/theta_max)

theta_min.description: Boundary condition at θ=0 (angular start boundary)

theta_max.description: Boundary condition at θ=theta_range (angular end boundary)

type.description: Boundary condition type: 'dirichlet', 'neumann', 'periodic', or 'robin'. For periodic BC with value<0, anti-periodic BC is applied (f(θ=0) = -f(θ=θ_range))

value.description: Boundary condition value. For Dirichlet: fixed Az value. For Neumann: normal derivative. For periodic: >=0 normal periodic, <0 anti-periodic

alpha.description: Robin BC: coefficient for Az term (α·Az + β·∂Az/∂n = γ). Default: 1.0 (Dirichlet-like when β=0)

gamma.description: Robin BC: right-hand side value (α·Az + β·∂Az/∂n = γ). Default: 0.0

value_profile.description: v1.6 domain decomposition: path to a CSV of per-θ Dirichlet values (length ntheta, theta-index order) that overrides the scalar 'value' along a polar radial boundary. Used for spatially-varying transmission conditions; empty/absent falls back to the scalar value (backward compatible).

gamma_profile.description: v1.6 domain decomposition: path to a CSV of per-θ Robin γ values (length ntheta, theta-index order) that overrides the scalar 'gamma' for a Robin polar boundary (α·Az + β·∂Az/∂n = γ). Empty/absent falls back to the scalar gamma (backward compatible).

domain_decomposition.description: v1.6 domain decomposition (optimized Schwarz, POLAR only). Opt-in variable-resolution ACCURACY mode: keep the air gap / saturated zone FINE, coarsen smooth radial bands on their own uniform grid, coupled by symmetric Robin transmission iterated to consistency. NOT a speed default — uniform downsampling is faster; use when full-resolution gap accuracy matters (e.g. final-ranking / verification). Disabled unless 'enabled: true' with at least one band.
domain_decomposition.example:
domain_decomposition:
  enabled: true
  bands:
    - [0, 52, 4, 4]      # bore: coarsen 4x (smooth)
    - [52, 330, 1, 1]    # active band (gap/teeth/coils): keep FINE
    - [330, 450, 4, 4]   # deep yoke: coarsen 4x (smooth)
  robin_p: 12.0
  overlap: 4
  max_outer: 8
  max_inner: 3
  tol: 1.0e-3

bands.description: Radial bands, each [c0, c1, cf_r, cf_theta]: column range [c0,c1) in radial pixel indices, radial coarsen factor cf_r, theta coarsen factor cf_theta. cf=1 keeps the band FINE (use across the air gap / saturated active region). cf_theta=1 = r-only coarsening (preserves theta-varying slots/magnets). RULE: band interfaces (c0/c1) should fall in IRON, and the air gap must stay inside a fine band — interfaces in air or coils diverge.

robin_p.description: Robin transmission coefficient α for the inter-band interfaces (α·Az + β·∂Az/∂n = γ, β=1). Default 12.0 (validated). Interfaces should sit in iron for robust convergence.

overlap.description: Band overlap in FINE columns: each band is extended ±overlap·cf_r columns past its core before solving. A larger overlap helps convergence when an interface sits near a high-gradient zone (e.g. straddling the air gap, put the gap inside the overlap so the Robin trace lands in iron). Default 4.

max_outer.description: Maximum number of Schwarz outer sweeps. The DD usually reaches its flux accuracy within ~2-5 sweeps (the field error plateaus at the coarsening floor). Default 20.

max_inner.description: Maximum nonlinear subdomain iterations per Schwarz sweep. Default 3 distributes nonlinear relaxation across sweeps; <=0 restores the much slower fully nested legacy behaviour. A final uncapped polish sweep is always run.

tol.description: Convergence tolerance on the relative Schwarz residual ||G - G_prev|| / ||G||. The sweep stops early when the residual falls below tol (or at max_outer). Default 2.0e-3.

relax.description: Outer under-relaxation factor ω in (0,1]. 1.0 = none. Use ω<1 (e.g. 0.7) to damp a 2-cycle oscillation when an interface sits in a high-gradient zone. Default 1.0.

initial_az_path.description: v1.6 warm start: path to a raw float64 Az file used as the initial Newton-Krylov iterate (skips the linear init guess). Mainly for the DD outer loop / restarting a sweep; absent = cold start.

boundary_conditions.description: Boundary conditions for Cartesian coordinates (4 edges)

materials.description: Material definitions (any material name is allowed)
materials.example:
materials:
  air:
    rgb: [255, 255, 255]
    mu_r: 1.0
    jz: 0.0
  iron:
    rgb: [128, 128, 128]
    mu_r: 1000.0
    jz: 0.0
    calc_force: true

rgb.description: RGB color for material identification in input image [R, G, B]

mu_r.description: Relative permeability (dimensionless). Supports: constant, formula (quotes optional, with $H, $dx/$dy for Cartesian, $dr/$dtheta for polar, and user-defined $variables), or table [[H_values], [mu_r_values]]. Predefined constants: pi, e, mu0 (vacuum permeability = 4π×10⁻⁷ H/m)

jz.description: Current density [A/m²]. Supports: constant, formula (quotes optional), or array. Formula variables: $step, $dx/$dy (Cartesian), $dr/$dtheta (polar), $N (pixel count), $A (area [m²]), and user-defined $variables. Predefined constants: pi, e, mu0 (4π×10⁻⁷ H/m)

calc_force.description: Calculate Maxwell stress force on this material (true/false)

anti_aliasing.description: Enable anti-aliasing interpolation for gradient pixels at material boundaries. Uses harmonic mean of μ based on RGB distance ratio

preset.description: Reference to a material preset defined in material_presets section

material_presets.description: User-defined material presets for reuse. Define B-H curves or formulas once, reference by name

flux_linkage.description: Flux linkage definitions. Each entry is either a point-to-point path (Φ = Az(end) - Az(start)) or an area-averaged material definition. With both materials, Φ = mean(Az over material_a) - mean(Az over material_b). For an antiperiodic half-period model, either side may be omitted: material_a alone gives +mean(Az), and material_b alone gives -mean(Az). Cartesian uses uniform cell area; polar uses r-weighted physical area.
flux_linkage.example:
flux_linkage:
  - name: phase_U          # paired material sections
    material_a: coil_U_pos
    material_b: coil_U_neg
  - name: phase_V_half     # one visible section in a half-period model
    material_a: coil_V_pos
  - name: phase_W_half
    material_b: coil_W_neg
  - name: phase_path       # point-to-point variant
    start: [0.01, 0.05]
    end:   [0.01, 0.15]

name.description: Name identifier for flux linkage path

start.description: Start point coordinates [x, y] in physical units [m] for flux linkage path variant

end.description: End point coordinates [x, y] in physical units [m] for flux linkage path variant

material_a.description: v1.5/Phase B.3 — material name for the +Az side of a flux_linkage entry (cartesian only). Resolved to the material's RGB pixels at parse time.

material_b.description: v1.5/Phase B.3 — material name for the -Az side of a flux_linkage entry (cartesian only). Resolved to the material's RGB pixels at parse time.

transient.description: v1.6.1 transient analysis. Prefer slides: for motion; legacy single-slide keys remain compatible. Decimal/exponent band bounds are physical metres, integer bounds are pixel indices. Cartesian supports multiple slides; polar currently applies slides[0].
transient.example:
transient:
  enabled: true
  total_steps: 100
  parallel_chunks: 3
  enable_sliding: true
  slides:
    - name: rotor
      direction: vertical
      region_start: 0.05
      region_end: 0.09
      angle_deg: 0.25
      pixels_per_step: 1
      wrap_mode: auto

slides.description: v1.6.1 list of independent band/rectangle slides. Cartesian fully supports multiple entries; polar currently applies slides[0] only and warns about additional entries.
slides.example:
slides:
  - name: rotor
    direction: vertical
    region_start: 100
    region_end: 400
    pixels_per_step: 5

direction.description: v1.5/Phase B.2 — direction of a slide region: 'vertical' (slides rows) or 'horizontal' (slides cols)

region_start.description: Sliding-band start. Decimal/exponent literal = physical metres; integer literal = legacy pixel index. In polar coordinates metre bounds must lie on the r axis.

region_end.description: Sliding-band end in the same authored units as region_start. Inverted metre bounds are swapped and out-of-mesh bounds are clamped with warnings.

pixels_per_step.description: v1.5/Phase B.2 — circular-shift amount per step. Negative values reverse direction. Different slides in the same yaml can use different magnitudes / signs.

angle_rad.description: Polar physical rotation per step [rad]. Takes precedence over angle_deg and pixels_per_step and is resolved to theta pixels for the current mesh.

angle_deg.description: Polar physical rotation per step [deg]. Used when angle_rad is absent; overrides pixels_per_step.

wrap_mode.description: v1.5/Phase B.5 — what happens to content (and to per-cell source-term polarity) at the slide-wrap seam. 'periodic': circular shift, identity wraps unchanged. 'antiperiodic': circular shift + flip jz / magnetisation sign on cells that crossed the seam (consistent with anti-periodic theta BC). 'vacuum': no wrap; vacated cells get vacuum_rgb (consistent with Dirichlet BC). 'auto' (default): pick based on the perpendicular boundary's BC type.

vacuum_rgb.description: v1.5/Phase B.5 — RGB triple [R,G,B] used to fill vacated cells when wrap_mode is 'vacuum'. Default is [255,255,255] (white = air). Set to the RGB of whichever 'background' material you defined under materials:.

kind.description: v1.5/Phase B.6 — slide region shape. 'band' (default) slides a vertical or horizontal strip of the image (direction + region_start/end + pixels_per_step). 'rectangle' cuts a 2-D box (rect + dx + dy) and translates it; pixels that walk off the image edge are dropped, the vacated source region is filled with vacuum_rgb, and multiple rectangles overlay in slides-list order at any colliding destination.

rect.description: v1.5/Phase B.6 — rectangle slide initial position: [x_start, y_start, x_end, y_end] in image pixel coordinates (origin = top-left).

dx.description: v1.5/Phase B.6 — rectangle slide x-velocity per step. Either a numeric constant or a tinyexpr formula. $name tokens are globally substituted at load time; $step is bound per evaluation. Fractional values are accumulated in float space so e.g. 0.5 produces alternating 0 / 1 shifts rather than rounding to zero.

dy.description: v1.5/Phase B.6 — rectangle slide y-velocity per step. Same evaluation rules as dx.

enable_sliding.description: Enable image sliding for rotor motion simulation (true/false)

parallel_chunks.description: Split the sweep into K contiguous chunks solved concurrently (each chunk keeps the mu warm-start amortization; each chunk's first step is cold). Speedup is memory-bandwidth-bound (~1.9x measured at K=3). 1 = sequential (default).

slide_region_start.description: Start of the sliding band. DECIMAL literal (e.g. 0.005) = physical METRES, converted via the mesh (polar: radius from r_start; cartesian: x or y). INTEGER literal (e.g. 110) = pixel index (legacy). vertical slide bounds columns, horizontal bounds rows.

slide_region_end.description: End of the sliding band. DECIMAL literal = physical METRES (see slide_region_start); INTEGER literal = pixel index (legacy).

slide_angle_rad.description: Legacy single-slide polar rotation per step [rad]. Takes precedence over slide_angle_deg and slide_pixels_per_step.

slide_angle_deg.description: Legacy single-slide polar rotation per step [deg]. Overrides slide_pixels_per_step when slide_angle_rad is absent.

export_fields.description: Optional transient output allow-list. Empty/absent exports every field for backward compatibility.
export_fields.example: export_fields: [Az, Mu, H, Jz, InputImg, Forces, EnergyDensity]

nonlinear_solver.description: Nonlinear solver configuration for materials with field-dependent permeability μ(H)
nonlinear_solver.example:
nonlinear_solver:
  enabled: true
  solver_type: newton-krylov
  max_iterations: 100
  tolerance: 1.0e-3
  verbose: false
  eisenstat_walker:
    enabled: true

eisenstat_walker.description: [Phase BC, v1.5.1+] Eisenstat-Walker inexact-Newton forcing for the inner AMGCL CG tolerance. When enabled, η_k = γ·(‖R_k‖/‖R_{k-1}‖)^α clipped to [eta_min, eta_max] — lets the inner CG stop early in outer iters where the Newton residual is still loose, avoiding wasteful 1e-6 inner accuracy. Headline measured win on IEEJ-D IPMSM: 377 s → 153 s (-59 %, 2.5× speedup). Default off; turn on for any nonlinear run.
eisenstat_walker.example:
eisenstat_walker:
  enabled: true
  gamma: 0.9
  alpha: 2.0
  eta_min: 1.0e-6
  eta_max: 0.1

gamma.description: [eisenstat_walker] γ in η_k = γ·(‖R_k‖/‖R_{k-1}‖)^α. Default 0.9. Lower (e.g. 0.7) tightens the inner tolerance for more accurate Newton steps at the cost of inner-CG work.

alpha.description: [eisenstat_walker] α exponent in η_k. Choice 1 (α=1+sqrt(5)/2 ≈ 1.62) is the classical Eisenstat-Walker 1996 form; Choice 2 (α=2) is more aggressive — recommended when the Newton step is well-aligned with the descent direction. Default 2.0.

eta_min.description: [eisenstat_walker] Floor of the inner-CG tolerance. Default 1.0e-6 — matches SOLVER_TOLERANCE so the tightened steps still hit the linear solver's accuracy floor.

eta_max.description: [eisenstat_walker] Cap (and initial value for iter 0) of the inner-CG tolerance. Default 0.1. Larger values let early outer iters use very loose inner solves; too large (>0.5) starts to break Newton step quality.

solver_type.description: Nonlinear solver algorithm: 'picard' (simple fixed-point) or 'newton-krylov' (recommended baseline).

anderson.description: Opt-in safeguarded Anderson acceleration for Newton-Krylov (default beta 0.3). Keep it disabled unless comparing convergence against the stable Newton-Krylov baseline. Plain solver_type: picard remains unaccelerated.

depth.description: Anderson acceleration history depth (integer >= 1; typically 3-10). Larger history uses more memory and can make extrapolation less robust.

beta.description: Anderson: finite mixing parameter in [0.0, 1.0] (1.0 = full Anderson). Newton-Krylov uses 0.3 when omitted. Robin BC: coefficient for ∂Az/∂n term (α·Az + β·∂Az/∂n = γ), set >0 for external reluctance

max_iterations.description: Maximum number of nonlinear iterations. Reaching this limit retains diagnostic output and completes with exit code 2 as a nonlinear-convergence warning; the result is not converged, but execution did not fail.

tolerance.description: Required relative residual norm. Smaller is stricter and may need substantially more iterations. Results are accepted only below this value; compare field maps only when both runs converged.

line_search_c.description: Armijo parameter for sufficient decrease condition (Newton-Krylov only, typically 1e-4)

line_search_alpha_init.description: Initial step length (Newton-Krylov only, 1.0 = full Newton step)

line_search_alpha_min.description: Minimum step length safety bound (Newton-Krylov only)

line_search_rho.description: Backtracking factor (Newton-Krylov only, 0 < rho < 1, default 0.5, higher = more aggressive)

line_search_max_trials.description: Maximum number of backtracking trials (Newton-Krylov only)

line_search_adaptive.description: Enable adaptive initial step length (Newton-Krylov only, recommended for better convergence)

export_convergence.description: Export convergence history to CSV file (true/false)

B-H.description:
B-H curve for a material. Three formats supported:
  Normal curve (H >= 0):  [[H,...],[B,...]] [A/m, T]
  Demagnetization curve (H <= 0):  [[-Hcb,...,0],[0,...,Br]] — Br and mu_r extracted from slope at H=0
  Formula:  "expression with $H" [A/m → T]
For normal/formula: μr(H)=(B(H)-Br)/(μ₀H) is derived internally. If H[0]=0 and B[0]≠0, residual Br is detected. Supports $H, user-defined $variables, constants: pi, e, mu0 (4π×10⁻⁷ H/m)
B-H.example:
# Normal B-H (soft magnet):
B-H: [[0, 100, 500, 2000, 5000],
      [0, 0.30, 1.00, 1.50, 1.70]]
# Demagnetization curve (permanent magnet, second quadrant):
B-H: [[-960000, -700000, -400000, 0],
      [0,       0.4,     0.9,    1.27]]
# Formula:
B-H: "mu0 * 1000 * $H"

bh_type.description:
Classification flag for B-H curves when B(H=0) ≠ 0. Controls how the solver interprets a non-zero intercept:
  auto   (default) — infer: if B(0)≠0, treat as permanent magnet (demagnetization curve)
  magnet — always treat as demagnetization curve: extract Br and recoil μr, use STATIC permeability
  soft   — treat as soft magnet with a bias offset: build magnetization TABLE for H≥0, ignore B(0)

magnetization.description: Permanent magnet magnetization model. Implements equivalent magnetization current Jz_mag=∇×M. Specify Br (preferred) or Hc, then pattern and direction parameters

pattern.description:
Magnetization pattern type:
  parallel — uniform direction (specify angle)
  radial — outward (or inward via direction) from center (cx, cy)
  tangential — counter-clockwise (or clockwise via direction) from center (cx, cy)
  halbach_continuous — continuous Halbach array (p, cx, cy, orientation_offset); M ∝ cos((p/2)·θ)
  polar_anisotropy — pole-following easy axis from p orientation centres OJ on a pitch circle (p, R_pc, cx, cy, orientation_offset); see Kano 2025 §3.2
  radial_array — alternating radial-out / radial-in per pole sector (axially-magnetised SPM, p sectors)
  parallel_array — uniform parallel within each pole sector along the sector mid-axis, alternating per pole (axially-magnetised IPM with rectangular magnets, p sectors)
  custom — user expression (Mx, My)

direction.description: Sign / orientation flag for radial, tangential, radial_array, and parallel_array patterns. 'outward' (default) puts the first pole positive / radial pointing out; 'inward' flips the sign. Use to express the second half of an NS alternation when each side is its own colour, or to set the initial pole of an array pattern.

Br.description: Residual flux density [T] for permanent magnets (remanence). Preferred over Hc — directly available from datasheets. Internally converts to M0=Br/μ₀. Can also be derived automatically from B-H: data when H[0]=0

Hc.description: Coercive force [A/m] for permanent magnets. Use Br: instead when the remanence value is known. When B-H: is defined with remanence and no Hc:/Br:, M0 is derived from B-H automatically

p.description: Number of POLES for 'halbach_continuous', 'polar_anisotropy', 'radial_array', and 'parallel_array' patterns. A 4-pole machine uses p=4. Even values give a closed NS alternation (odd values are accepted but the M field does not close at θ=2π). For sector-based patterns the number of sectors equals p with each spanning 2π/p radians (360/p degrees). halbach_continuous internally uses p/2 in its M ∝ cos((p/2)·θ) formula. polar_anisotropy uses p OJ centres on the pitch circle.

R_pc.description: Pitch circle radius [m] for 'polar_anisotropy' pattern. Defines the reference circle for the orientation-centre points OJ (Kano 2025 §3.2). Typical choice: Kn=Fn/Rm in [1.0, 4.0]; Kn≈1.6 gives near-sinusoidal gap density (THD<1%). Here Fn=R_pc and Rm is the magnet outer radius

orientation_offset.description: Pole-structure rotation offset [deg] for 'halbach_continuous', 'polar_anisotropy', 'radial_array', and 'parallel_array' patterns. Rotates the first pole / OJ around (cx, cy). Solver default is 0 (sector 0 spans [0°, 360°/p]); the WebUI Detect Colors UI seeds -180/p (sector 0 centred on θ=0, i.e. cardinal-aligned) when the user first picks a sector pattern. Distinct from the transient slide rotation tracked by the solver between time steps.
orientation_offset.example: orientation_offset: -45    # p=4, sector 0 centred on θ=0

Mx.description: Custom magnetization x-component expression for 'custom' pattern. Available variables: x, y, r, theta (atan2(y-cy,x-cx)), Hc

My.description: Custom magnetization y-component expression for 'custom' pattern. Available variables: x, y, r, theta (atan2(y-cy,x-cx)), Hc

export.description: Result export configuration. v1.6.1 defaults are format=tiff, precision=double, async=true, queue depth=4, DEFLATE and floating-point predictor. Partial export blocks inherit these same defaults.
export.example:
export:
  format: tiff
  precision: double
  async: true
  tiff:
    compression: deflate
    predictor: 3

format.description: Output format: 'csv' (legacy text, large), 'tiff' (IEEE 754 binary, compressed), or 'both' (write both, ~3x slower writes but maximal compatibility while WebUI/tools catch up).

precision.description: Numeric precision for TIFF output. 'double' = full IEEE 754 64-bit (no information loss vs. solver state). 'float' = 32-bit, halves the file size. Default 'double'.

async.description: Run file writes on a background worker thread so the solver does not wait on disk. Output ordering is preserved. Default true; set false only for synchronous-I/O diagnostics.

async_queue_depth.description: Maximum number of pending write jobs before the solver thread blocks (backpressure). Valid range 1..16. Bigger = more overlap, more transient memory. Default 4.

compression.description: libtiff compression scheme: 'none' (1), 'lzw' (5), 'deflate' (8). Default 'deflate'; combined with predictor=3 it reduces double-precision field data ~3-5x without loss.

predictor.description: libtiff TIFFTAG_PREDICTOR. 1 = none (raw bytes), 2 = horizontal differencing (good for integer images), 3 = floating-point predictor (required for double/float to get meaningful compression). Default 3.

mu_r: 1.05
magnetization:
  Br: 1.2
  pattern: parallel

domain_decomposition_template.name: Domain Decomposition - variable-resolution Schwarz (polar, opt-in accuracy mode)
domain_decomposition_template.snippet:
enabled: true
bands:
  - [0, 52, 4, 4]      # bore: coarsen 4x (smooth)
  - [52, 330, 1, 1]    # active band (gap/teeth/coils): keep FINE
  - [330, 450, 4, 4]   # deep yoke: coarsen 4x (smooth)
robin_p: 12.0          # Robin transmission coeff (interfaces should sit in iron)
overlap: 4
max_outer: 20
tol: 1.0e-3
# relax: 0.7           # under-relaxation if an interface oscillates

lib_file_template.name: Material Library Template
lib_file_template.snippet:
material_presets:
  my_soft_material:
    B-H: "mu0 * 1000 * $H"
  my_magnet:
    mu_r: 1.05
    magnetization:
      Br: 1.27
      pattern: parallel
      angle: 0

lib_preset_magnet_parallel.name: Preset - Permanent Magnet (parallel)
lib_preset_magnet_parallel.snippet:
mu_r: 1.05
magnetization:
  Br: 1.27
  pattern: parallel
  angle: 0

lib_preset_magnet_demag.name: Preset - Permanent Magnet (demagnetization curve)
lib_preset_magnet_demag.snippet:
B-H: [[-960000, -700000, -400000, 0],
      [0, 0.4, 0.9, 1.27]]
bh_type: magnet
magnetization:
  pattern: parallel
  angle: 0

export_tiff_template.name: Export - TIFF (double, async)
export_tiff_template.snippet:
format: tiff
precision: double
async: true
tiff:
  compression: deflate
  predictor: 3

export_both_template.name: Export - both CSV+TIFF (legacy interoperability)
export_both_template.snippet:
format: both
precision: double
async: true
tiff:
  compression: deflate
  predictor: 3

polar_2d_motor.name: Polar 2D Motor Analysis
polar_2d_motor.description: Template for 2D motor analysis in polar coordinates
polar_2d_motor.content:
coordinate_system: polar

polar_domain:
  r_start: 0.222
  r_end: 0.278
  r_orientation: horizontal
  theta_range: 1.0471975512  # π/3

polar_boundary_conditions:
  inner:
    type: dirichlet
    value: 0.0
  outer:
    type: dirichlet
    value: 0.0
  theta_min:
    type: periodic
    value: 0.0  # Use value: -1.0 for anti-periodic BC
  theta_max:
    type: periodic
    value: 0.0  # Use value: -1.0 for anti-periodic BC

materials:
  air:
    rgb: [255, 255, 255]
    mu_r: 1.0
    jz: 0.0

  iron_stator:
    rgb: [128, 128, 128]
    mu_r: 100.0
    jz: 0.0
    calc_force: false

  iron_rotor:
    rgb: [100, 100, 100]
    mu_r: 500.0
    jz: 0.0
    calc_force: true

transient:
  enabled: true
  enable_sliding: true
  total_steps: 167
  slide_direction: vertical
  slide_region_start: 0.222   # decimal = metres (rotor-side band)
  slide_region_end: 0.25
